subject: Computer Networking
title: DKIM — Digital Signatures
description: Learn DKIM — Digital Signatures in one minute.

hook.text: SPF checks the server. DKIM checks the message itself. It signs the email so tampering is detectable.

buildup.text: The sending server signs key headers and the body with a private key. A DKIM-Signature header is added.

discovery.text: The receiver fetches the public key from DNS and verifies the signature. If it matches, nothing was altered.

twist.text: DKIM survives forwarding. The signature stays intact because it's tied to content, not the sending IP.

climax.text: Gmail, Outlook, and Yahoo all require DKIM. Without it, your emails may land in the spam folder.

punchline.text: DKIM proves the email is authentic and unmodified. Digital trust.

quiz.question: Where does the receiving server find the DKIM public key?
options: From the sender's SMTP server directly

details.summary: DomainKeys Identified Mail adds a cryptographic signature to emails that proves the message was sent by the domain and was not altered in transit. The sending server signs the message with a private key and publishes the public key in DNS for receivers to verify authenticity.
details.whyItMatters: DKIM provides cryptographic proof that an email is genuine and unmodified. It is the strongest technical defense against email forgery and tampering.
takeaways: DKIM signs emails with a private key held by the sending domain
Receivers verify signatures using the public key published in DNS
DKIM detects both sender forgery and message tampering

faq.question: What does a DKIM signature actually verify?
faq.answer: It verifies that specific email headers and the body were not modified after the sending server signed them. It also proves the message was sent by a server holding the domain's private key. This prevents both forgery and tampering during transit.

faq.question: Can DKIM be defeated?
faq.answer: DKIM can break when mailing lists or forwarding services modify the message body or headers. Replay attacks can resend a legitimately signed message. DKIM alone does not tell receivers what to do with unsigned messages. DMARC adds policy enforcement on top of DKIM.
